intended_object: The i-th letter of a based oriented Gauss code: the crossing label visited at position i together with its over/under status (e.g. O3/U3 in Gauss-word notation). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (Lickorish, Ch. 1).
explanation: The body is exactly (D.visit i, D.over i), the pair (crossing label, over flag) at visit i, as the docstring says. Together, the structure fields visit_eq_iff (fibres of visit are partner pairs) and over_partner (opposite over/under within a pair) make this map a bijection Fin (2n) ≃ Fin n × Bool. The library proves this immediately afterwards (visitData_bijective, visitDataEquiv), matching the textbook fact that each crossing is visited exactly once over and once under. It only reads off fields of the library's own Gauss-code structure, so it is not too narrow, and Mathlib has no Gauss-code notion that it could duplicate.
